national_raw_news.content: BRICS nations have unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration on the First day of the BRICS Summit 2026, being held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed to adopt the declaration at the end of the session on the first day of the summit. In his closing remarks, the Prime Minister noted that the New Delhi Declaration adopted today provides a clear direction for the shared resolve of the member countries. He added that it is now their shared responsibility to translate these resolutions into tangible results. The Prime Minister said that today’s discussion makes it evident that the changing world cannot be steered by outdated institutions and underlined that reforms are essential in representation, responsiveness, and rule-making. Mr Modi said that the leaders also emphasised that the Global South must have equal participation in the development of future technologies and the rules governing them. He emphasised that the gap between decisions and their outcomes must be bridged through partnership and collective action. The Prime Minister also expressed his gratitude to the leaders for their valuable contributions, constructive spirit and commitment as the BRICS Chair. To mark the 20 years of BRICS, two commemorative postage stamps were also released by the leaders of the member countries on this occasion. Earlier in his opening remarks on the first day of the session, which was based on inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism, Mr Modi proposed a BRICS Continuity and Implementation Mechanism to ensure that the grouping’s institutional momentum is maintained despite the Chairship changing every year. In his opening remarks at today’s session of the BRICS Summit 2026, which is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Mr Modi said the mechanism would enable follow-up of all initiatives and outcomes through the Troika. The Prime Minister said BRICS countries will have to work on a new and ambitious agenda for the next 20 years. He said the process must begin with the grouping’s own working system. The Prime Minister also proposed to establish a Seafarers Emergency Support Network to connect the maritime authorities and diplomatic missions of relevant countries to facilitate assistance during difficult times. Mr Modi observed that seafarers make a massive contribution to global trade, yet they often find themselves lacking support during difficult times. Mr Modi said the time has come to translate the unity and consensus among BRICS countries into concrete outcomes on the global stage. He stressed that BRICS members respect one another and move forward through consensus. He said the grouping is not working against anyone, but is moving forward with the approach of taking everyone along. The Prime Minister described this year’s BRICS Summit as a historic milestone, noting that the grouping is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year. He said BRICS is at its coming-of-age moment and has established its distinct identity on the global stage over the past two decades. Mr Modi said India’s Chairship of BRICS is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach. He said Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability have been India’s foremost priorities as Chair. Guided by these priorities, India has laid special emphasis on connecting BRICS cooperation directly with the common people. The Prime Minister noted that with this vision, more than 350 meetings were organised, and India had the privilege of welcoming delegations across nearly 30 cities in the country. In his address, the Prime Minister noted that the Global South stands in the front row of global crises but in the back row of decision-making. He emphasised transforming this ‘pyramid of privilege’ into a ‘platform of partnership’. In this context, the Prime Minister proposed to jointly formulate 10 proposals for global governance reform, aiming to shape them into a BRICS reform roadmap by the time of the next Summit. On the issue of reform in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), the Prime Minister emphasised that reform of the UNSC can no longer be postponed and negotiations on this matter must be linked to a definite time frame and clear outcomes. He said, similarly, voting power, leadership positions, and policy priorities within financial institutions must align with today’s economic realities. national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 76 PM Modi and President of China, Xi Jinping stress for strategic, long term perspective of ties in...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President of China, Xi Jinping today reaffirmed that India and China should take a strategic and long term perspective of their ties and that differences should not become disputes. During their bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit, the two leaders welcomed the steady progress in India-China bilateral relations since their last meeting in Tianjin in August last year. Prime Minister Modi highlighted that both sides must be guided by three mutuals – mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest. He emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas remain an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations. He underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues. The two leaders expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question proceeding from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two peoples. External Affairs Ministry said in a statement that the two leaders took note of the progress in people-to-people ties and underscored the need to further promote cultural exchanges, business linkages and greater mobility between the two countries. On economic and trade relations, they underlined the need to address each other’s concerns, including structural trade imbalance and supply chain issues, and facilitation of meaningful and predictable market access. The two leaders agreed that both sides must continue to expand common ground on regional and global issues and in addressing challenges. Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Modi held a series of bilateral meetings with leaders of BRICS countries.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 211 PM Narendra Modi holds bilateral talks with BRICS leaders
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a series of bilateral meetings with his counterparts from Ethiopia, Malaysia and Vietnam as well as the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi. The Prime Minister began his bilateral engagements by holding talks with his Ethiopian counterpart Dr Abiy Ahmed Ali. The Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement that the two leaders held discussions aimed at further strengthening the bilateral Strategic Partnership. Both the leaders reviewed progress across key sectors, including economic cooperation, defence and security partnership, and capacity building. The meeting built on Prime Minister Modi’s historic visit to Addis Ababa in December 2025. The two leaders also exchanged perspectives on regional and international developments of mutual interest and reaffirmed their commitment to close cooperation in multilateral fora. During the meeting, Prime Minister Modi expressed appreciation for Ethiopia’s participation in the 18th BRICS Summit and noted that its presence helped in reinforcing the collective voice of the Global South. The Prime Minister also held bilateral talks with his Malaysian counterpart, Anwar Ibrahim. During the meeting, the two leaders reviewed the progress in bilateral cooperation across a range of areas, including trade and investment, defence and security and people-to-people ties. They also took stock of the outcomes of Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Malaysia in February this year. Mr Modi appreciated Malaysia’s continued support in strengthening ASEAN-India relations. The leaders exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest and expressed their continued commitment to advancing the India-Malaysia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. In the meeting with his Vietnamese counterpart, Le Minh Hung, Prime Minister Modi welcomed Vietnam’s participation in the BRICS Summit as a Partner Country. The Ministry of External Affairs said that the meeting provided an opportunity for both leaders to review the progress made in bilateral ties, which were elevated to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during the State Visit of Vietnamese President To Lam to India in May this year. Both leaders also exchanged views on various regional and global issues of mutual importance and reaffirmed the commitment to further strengthening their partnership. India and Vietnam share a time-tested friendship rooted in shared civilisational heritage, mutual trust and understanding. Vietnam is a key pillar of India’s Act East Policy and an important partner in India’s broader engagement with Southeast Asia. The Prime Minister also held bilateral talks with the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. During the meeting, both sides reiterated the significance of the India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which is built on strong political, cultural, commercial, energy, and people-to-people relations. Both sides also agreed that the two countries will continue to work closely to advance shared interests and priorities and further strengthen BRICS cooperation. The two leaders positively noted the announcement by UAE’s International Holding Company to invest in the development of a 11.5 billion US Dollar integrated greenfield aluminium project in Odisha. The project is expected to position Odisha as a global aluminium manufacturing hub.

national_raw_news.title: Archery Premier League to be held in Hyderabad from October 8 to 18 1 hour ago 9
national_raw_news.content: The Archery Premier League (APL) is set for a bigger second season, with 36 of India’s leading archers set to compete alongside 12 international stars from 10 countries in Hyderabad from October 8 to 18. The expanded field brings together Olympic medallists, world champions, World Cup winners and some of the biggest names in the sport, adding further international flavour to the six-franchise competition. Four-time Olympian Deepika Kumari and World Championship silver medallist Atanu Das headline India’s recurve contingent, with reigning Asian champion Dhiraj Bommadevara also part of the field. The compound section features multi-time World Cup and Asian Games champion Jyothi Surekha Vennam, former World No. 1 Abhishek Verma and former World Champion Ojas Pravin Deotale. The international contingent is led by Tokyo 2020 Olympic champion Mete Gazoz of Türkiye, Paris 2024 bronze medallist Casey Kaufhold of the United States, Brazil’s World No. 1 Marcus D’Almeida and Great Britain’s World No. 2 Ella Gibson. Dutch compound star Mike Schloesser, a former World Champion and four-time World Cup Final winner, will also compete. The league will also feature all 12 members of India’s Asian Games-bound archery squad, giving the APL added relevance ahead of the country’s campaign in Aichi-Nagoya later this month. Among those entering the league for the first time are World Championships silver medallist Rajat Chauhan, World Cup stage gold medallist Ridhi, World University Games gold medallist Kushal Dalal and junior national champion Kirti Sharma. The second season will retain one of the league’s most distinctive features – its 15-second shot clock. Five seconds quicker than the standard Olympic timing, the format is designed to place greater emphasis on speed, decision-making and composure under pressure. Initiated by the Archery Association of India with the support of the Government of Telangana, the league will feature six mixed-gender franchise teams competing across the Recurve and Compound categories. The 11-day tournament will be held at People’s Plaza on Hyderabad’s Necklace Road. Rajputana Royals won the inaugural edition, which also generated significant digital engagement among younger audiences.

national_raw_news.title: India’s 2026 BRICS Presidency broadening historically strong oil-related ties with Gulf, says Report 5 hours ago 58
national_raw_news.content: India’s 2026 BRICS Presidency is broadening historically strong oil-related ties with the Gulf into a wider partnership spanning investment, technology, food security, clean energy and regional stability, a report has said. The report published in a daily published from UAE said energy ties remain the foundation of the relationship at the 18th BRICS Summit, but cooperation is expanding into new strategic areas. During Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the UAE this year, both the countries deepened collaboration on crude oil, LNG and LPG, and agreed to increase UAE participation in India’s strategic petroleum reserves and explored strategic gas reserves. Another area of co-operation is food-security which can link Gulf demand with India’s agricultural and food-processing capabilities. Investment in storage, logistics and reliable supply chains can be explored, the report noted. Highlighting the timing of the event, the report said that regional tensions have renewed attention on energy security, maritime trade and safe shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while Gulf states diversify their economies, invest in advanced technology and strengthen commercial links with Asia. The Gulf is represented in the expanded BRICS through Saudi Arabia and the UAE, providing the bloc greater weight in the global energy and finance landscape. India-Gulf ties grew stronger in February this year, when the country signed terms of reference with GCC and formally launched negotiations for a comprehensive free trade agreement, covering Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

national_raw_news.title: SEBI proposes changes to methodology for calculating expiry-day settlement prices of index and stock derivatives 5 hours ago 69
national_raw_news.content: Markets regulator SEBI on Saturday proposed changes to the methodology for calculating expiry-day settlement prices of index and stock derivatives, following a review of the newly introduced closing auction session (CAS) framework. In a consultation paper, SEBI proposed two options for determining the settlement prices, a blended Volume Weighted Average Price – VWAP based on trades executed during the last 30 minutes of the continuous trading session – CTS, and the 10-minute CAS, or continuation of the existing CTS VWAP methodology. The proposals follow feedback received from market participants on the use of the CAS-determined closing price for settling derivative contracts on expiry. Determination of derivative settlement prices based on the closing price arrived at through CAS was among the significant areas of feedback received by SEBI. SEBI introduced the CAS framework in the equity cash segment from August 3 to determine the closing price of securities. Under the current framework, the closing price determined through CAS also serves as the basis for determining settlement prices of derivative contracts on expiry. The use of the CAS-determined closing price for expiry-day settlement of derivatives has been one of the key concerns raised by market participants, prompting Sebi to review the existing methodology. On 3rd September, SEBI had said it may propose changes to the methodology following the feedback and indicated that a consultation paper on the proposed framework was likely to be released in about a week. The proposed changes are aimed at addressing concerns around the use of the CAS-determined closing price as the basis for settling derivative contracts on expiry. The Securities and Exchange Board of India – SEBI has sought comments from stakeholders on the proposals till 3rd October.

national_raw_news.title: Inflows through FCNR-B reflect confidence in India’s macroeconomic fundamentals: RBI Governor 5 hours ago 61
national_raw_news.content: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said that inflows through the Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) [FCNR-B] and the other schemes have been ‘very robust’. In an interview with a private television channel, the RBI Governor said the strong inflows reflect confidence in India’s macroeconomic fundamentals and demonstrate the ability to attract foreign capital within a short period. On the surplus liquidity in the banking system, Malhotra said the Reserve Bank has enough tools at its disposal to manage liquidity and is prepared to use them as needed. He added that some of the surplus liquidity would be withdrawn over time through currency circulation, forex intervention and banks’ reserve requirements amid rising credit growth. Malhotra added that the central bank’s objective was to maintain appropriate liquidity conditions and keep the weighted average call rate aligned with the repo rate. The RBI Governor said the Monetary Policy Committee would reassess growth and inflation dynamics at its meeting next month amid rising prices of crude oil owing to the ongoing West Asia crisis. Sanjay Malhotra noted that the impact of higher crude prices on inflation would depend on the extent to which the increase is passed through to consumers. He said the government has to a great degree, absorbed and cushioned the shock; as a result, the Indian economy has weathered it well. On stronger-than-expected growth in the April to June quarter, the RBI Governor said it was not entirely surprising. He added that incoming corporate data was also pointing to firmer growth. The central bank saw no signs of overheating, including in consumption loans.

national_raw_news.title: Saragarhi Day observed in Punjab, tributes paid to martyrs of Battle of Saragarhi 6 hours ago 72
national_raw_news.content: In Punjab, on the occasion of Saragarhi Day today, tributes were paid to the martyrs of the Battle of Saragarhi at its memorial in Ferozepur. In Amritsar, Bhog of Akhand Path Sahib was performed at Saragarhi Gurdwara in the memory of 21 British-Indian Sikh soldiers. They gave their supreme sacrifice while fighting with 10,000 Afghan tribals to defend the Saragarhi Fort in Waziristan on September 12th, 1897. A state-level programme was organised at Ferozepur in which family members of the martyrs, army officers and a large number of people paid tribute to the brave soldiers. State Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudiyan honoured their family members on the occasion. The Battle of Saragarhi is an unprecedented battle in world military history. It was on this day, 129 years ago, when 21 brave Sikh soldiers under the leadership of Havaldar Ishar Singh of the Sikh Regiment fought to their last breath against the Afghan tribesmen in Samana village of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, presently in Pakistan. They killed hundreds of attacking tribesmen and foiled their attempts to capture the Saragarhi Fort. They were honoured with the highest Indian military bravery award of those days, the Indian Order of Merit. The award is presently equated to Paramvir Chakra.

A 13 member delegation comprising journalists from Srinagar along with PIB officials will take part in the tour. Ahead of the delegation’s departure, Director PIB Srinagar, Qazi Salman, briefed the participants on the objectives of the visit, urging them to make meaningful use of the interactions and interviews planned during their time in Chennai. The delegation is being led by Shahid Lone, Field Publicity Officer at CBC Anantnag, who will serve as Conducting Officer for the tour, with Ifham Ul Islam, Information Assistant at PIB Srinagar, also accompanying the group. The tour is designed to give the visiting journalists firsthand exposure to key Central Government institutions, projects and initiatives based in Chennai, with the aim of deepening their understanding of national level policies and how these are implemented on the ground in different parts of the country. During the visit, the delegation will tour various Central Government establishments and projects in the city and interact with senior officials to better understand their functioning and day to day operations. Addressing the delegation before departure, Qazi Salman congratulated the participants and expressed confidence that the visit would offer valuable opportunities for professional engagement and a better understanding of how Central Government institutions function beyond what journalists typically encounter in their regular regional coverage. The approved projects include a Parking-cum-Commercial Complex at Parade and a Multilevel Car Parking facility at SMGS Hospital, two locations that have long struggled with inadequate parking capacity relative to the volume of vehicular traffic and footfall they see on a daily basis.
